Existing wallet token allowance or caller-owned internal vault deposits are required; no new approval/permit/NFT-operator capability is admitted.

For WETH payment, pay() uses available PERIPHERY native ETH balance when sufficient, wrapping only the amount owed; this may include residual ETH, not just current msg.value. Excess native value is not automatically refunded. useVaultDeposit=true rejects this native-WETH branch; otherwise vault deposits are debited only from caller or ERC20 is pulled from caller. Other LP methods are nonpayable. No whole-balance wrap/sweep helper is admitted.

collect, drain, detach and portion require an actually minted LP NFT and existing owner/operator authorization through _verifyTokenIdAndGetLpNum. They target the pool encoded in that owned position, not an arbitrary supplied address, and supply fixed empty callback bytes. detach and portion mint new resulting LP NFTs to caller, including an authorized operator caller; do not assume the prior owner receives the new NFT. Receiver selects pool payout recipient.

Range edges are signed int256 values converted to tubs; portion liquidity is ABI bytes16 representing binary128 Quad, not a uint token amount. Invalid ranges, nonfinite/invalid Quad liquidity, insufficient positions or pool dependencies can revert. addLiquidity checks returned token amounts AGAINST MINIMA, not caller total-maximum-spend guards or a deadline. Exit/split methods have no explicit minimum payout or deadline. Pool pricing, fee accounting and rounding affect results; retained source does not attest every dynamic pool runtime or execution outcome.

tap is not admitted: it only decodes a caller-supplied tokenId and calls its embedded address without _requireOwned, operator authorization or factory-membership validation. It is LP accounting maintenance rather than a caller-capital exit. No callback entrypoint, loan/swap-forwarder execution, multicall, permit, new authorization, historical recovery or upgrade entrypoint is activated.

warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI inventory only; not live authorization, persistent runtime identity, backing, balances, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Only existing Ethereum infiniFi Gateway proxy 0x3f04b65ddbd87f9ce0a2e7eb24d80e7fb87625b5 is targeted, not individual token/controller contracts. Retained source-service proxy resolution binds InfiniFiGatewayV4 implementation 0x750136ac021a7149f0ee38141d0ba920cca1fc5d; newly retrieved full compilation ABI/source retains match grades, not exact_match. Registry-selected controllers, tokens, yieldSharing and governance roles remain mutable. Source inclusion is not independent runtime verification of every configured dependency.

All added routes are nonpayable and use existing caller input-token allowance to Gateway. USDC mint consumes USDC raw units; iUSD receipt amounts, siUSD shares, liUSD bucket shares and INFI governance-token amounts are different quantities. Choose intentional recipients. Internal Gateway/controller approvals are fixed financial plumbing over tokens held by Gateway, not a newly exposed wallet approval, delegate, signature or arbitrary executor capability.

mint and mintAndLock return iUSD receipt quantity; mintAndStake also returns receipt quantity rather than resulting siUSD shares. Combined stake/unstake routes distribute interpolation rewards and temporarily toggle the existing privileged staking-entry flag as the already-admitted stake/unstake do. They cannot accept caller execution targets or bytes. Most methods have no min-output or deadline; conversion rounding, fees, losses, controller caps/minima, bucket existence, and token/role/pause checks may revert or reduce receipts.

redeem pulls caller iUSD, validates pending-loss gate and invokes the fixed RedeemController. It can pay USDC immediately, partially pay and queue, or queue entirely; _minAssetsOut checks only immediately returned assets, so a positive minimum can forbid queue-only settlement. claimRedemption claims only caller queued redemption and pays caller. Queue order, liquidity, configured hooks, rounding and backing determine timing/outcomes. No automatic funding of the queue or full immediate cash-out is guaranteed.

liUSD creation and unstakeAndLock create locked receipt-token positions in configured duration buckets. startUnwinding consumes caller bucket shares and creates a timestamp-keyed unwinding position for caller; repeated same-timestamp positions may revert. Cancellation restores caller funds into a permitted lock bucket with duration at least the remaining unwind period, not liquid withdrawal. increaseUnwindingEpochs only lengthens configured duration, burning caller old bucket shares and minting new ones to caller. Tiny zero-value conversions may return after Gateway has already received shares, leaving input shares there rather than refunding automatically.

withdraw(uint256) settles only caller timestamp-keyed liUSD position; withdraw(address,uint256) can trigger another user matured position but payout remains fixed to that user. Both apply the pending-loss gate. Completion requires epoch maturity and sufficient configured dependency balances and uses current slashed/reward-adjusted accounting, not promised fixed principal or USDC. No arbitrary payout recipient override exists.

INFI lock/start/cancel/increase/complete methods use the configured governanceLockingController but are ordinary token lock lifecycle, NOT vote, multiVote, delegation, OFT bridging or signature authorization. lockInfi locks caller tokens; start and increase pull caller existing bucket shares; cancel is caller-position-only. completeInfiWithdrawal may finalize a named user position but pays that same user. Unlike the iUSD withdraw overloads, its Gateway body has no pending-iUSD-loss gate. ERC20Votes token transfer checkpoints are token bookkeeping, not caller-installed voting/delegation permission.

Gateway whenNotPaused and nonReentrant wrappers, controller ENTRY_POINT/LOCKED_TOKEN_MANAGER roles, unwinding arithmetic, interpolation availability and mutable reward/slash parameters remain enforced. MintController afterMint and RedeemController beforeRedeem hooks are administrator-configured, not caller calldata. No bridge, migrate, zap/executor, governance vote, approval, initialization, registry mutation or role/upgrade capability is admitted.

mint and mintAndLock return iUSD receipt quantity; mintAndStake also returns receipt quantity rather than resulting siUSD shares. redeem pulls caller iUSD, validates pending-loss gate and invokes the fixed RedeemController. It can pay USDC immediately, partially pay and queue, or queue entirely; _minAssetsOut checks only immediately returned assets, so a positive minimum can forbid queue-only settlement. claimRedemption claims only caller queued redemption and pays caller. Queue order, liquidity, configured hooks, rounding and backing determine timing/outcomes. No automatic funding of the queue or full immediate cash-out is guaranteed.

liUSD creation and unstakeAndLock create locked receipt-token positions in configured duration buckets. startUnwinding consumes caller bucket shares and creates a timestamp-keyed unwinding position for caller; repeated same-timestamp positions may revert. Cancellation restores caller funds into a permitted lock bucket with duration at least the remaining unwind period, not liquid withdrawal. increaseUnwindingEpochs only lengthens configured duration, burning caller old bucket shares and minting new ones to caller. Tiny zero-value conversions may return after Gateway has already received shares, leaving input shares there rather than refunding automatically.

withdraw(uint256) settles only caller timestamp-keyed liUSD position; withdraw(address,uint256) can trigger another user matured position but payout remains fixed to that user. Both apply the pending-loss gate. Completion requires epoch maturity and sufficient configured dependency balances and uses current slashed/reward-adjusted accounting, not promised fixed principal or USDC. No arbitrary payout recipient override exists.

INFI lock/start/cancel/increase/complete methods use the configured governanceLockingController but are ordinary token lock lifecycle, NOT vote, multiVote, delegation, OFT bridging or signature authorization. lockInfi locks caller tokens; start and increase pull caller existing bucket shares; cancel is caller-position-only. completeInfiWithdrawal may finalize a named user position but pays that same user. Unlike the iUSD withdraw overloads, its Gateway body has no pending-iUSD-loss gate. ERC20Votes token transfer checkpoints are token bookkeeping, not caller-installed voting/delegation permission.

Gateway whenNotPaused and nonReentrant wrappers, controller ENTRY_POINT/LOCKED_TOKEN_MANAGER roles, unwinding arithmetic, interpolation availability and mutable reward/slash parameters remain enforced. MintController afterMint and RedeemController beforeRedeem hooks are administrator-configured, not caller calldata. No bridge, migrate, zap/executor, governance vote, approval, initialization, registry mutation or role/upgrade capability is admitted.

warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory. All admitted calls are nonpayable and require zero native value.

Only Ethereum cDAI DInterest root 0x11b1c87983f881b3686f8b1171628357faa30038 is covered; exact current EIP1967 implementation 0x454007e5bae920258f25630dcd9c007ddd98c917 is upgradeable. Official published v4 frontend lists this pool; no older v3 deployment or generic fork ABI is substituted. Other Ethereum and Polygon pools and separate reward/gauge/funding-token deployment entrypoints are not admitted. The same cDAI root separately admits caller-funded floating-rate fund overloads and payInterestToFunders; those are distinct from fixed-term depositor savings and do not authorize direct funding-token dividend withdrawal.

New deposits and topups pull only msg.sender DAI; deposit ownership is minted as an NFT to caller. Topup, withdrawal and rollover require current NFT owner equal msg.sender, not merely approved operator. DAI and virtual-token amounts use 18 decimals; IDs are uint64 and maturity is Unix seconds. Metadata URI is NFT display data, not executable calldata.

New maturity must be in the future and within mutable MaxDepositPeriod; observed maximum was 31,556,952 seconds, minimum new deposit 100 DAI and GlobalDepositCap=0 (unlimited), not a perpetual availability assurance. Topups must be before maturity and quote at current rate. Both simple overloads set interest minimum to zero; minimumInterestAmount is checked BEFORE subtracting the interest fee, not a net-yield guarantee.

Own withdrawal uses positive virtual-token amount clamped to remaining balance (uint256 max withdraws all). early=true only before maturity forfeits interest and deducts mutable early-withdraw fee; early=false requires maturity. Fixed interest is accounting, not guaranteed repayment: money-market shortfall can reduce the actual stablecoin payout while the virtual claim is consumed. No caller payout minimum is available.

Rollover requires an already matured own deposit, consumes its whole virtual balance and creates a new caller-owned NFT while retaining principal in the money market; fee/funder settlements can still withdraw underlying. Partial withdrawals/topups update weighted rates and reward vesting; arithmetic truncation affects amounts. No explicit claim queue is present in these methods.

Rate oracle, fee model, money-market Compound dependency and MPH vesting/minter remain mutable or external dependencies; this record does not attest all dependency runtime identities or continued availability. Direct app/docs DNS failed in this environment; lifecycle prose was retrieved through indexed primary snippets and deployment attribution through the official published repository, with this access limitation retained.

Receiver chooses share ownership and must be intentional; use own wallet for own staking. Existing WETH allowance is required but no approval capability is added.

For staking-token accounting, ETH, WETH and spETH use 18-decimal base units. Vendored ERC4626 conversions use virtual assets and shares: shares=floor(assets*(totalSupply+1)/(totalAssets+1)); mint rounds assets up, withdraw rounds burned shares up, redeem rounds assets down. totalAssets uses updater-reported underlying and signed estimated rewards, not a raw onchain balance or backing proof. Share-rate estimates, losses and fees can change; entry methods have no minimum-shares or deadline parameter.

On the staking proxy, entry fee is taken from the gross shares before transfer to receiver (except pool caller), so returned/event shares and requested mint shares are gross, not guaranteed receiver-net shares. Admin may set depositFee up to 100 bps and rewardFee up to 2000 bps; current explorer reads depositFee=0 and rewardsFee=500. Whitelist is source-enforced on caller when enabled; current explorer reads whitelistEnabled=false, not a future access promise or jurisdiction/eligibility clearance.

On the staking proxy, withdraw(assets,receiver,owner) and redeem(shares,receiver,owner) are ASYNCHRONOUS requests, not immediate WETH/ETH payment: burn owner shares, decrease totalUnderlying and queue ETH owed in Withdrawal. If caller differs from owner it consumes owner share allowance. Critically the queue is keyed to caller, NOT owner: use owner=caller for own positions; allowance does not create an owner-keyed claim. The separately admitted liquid-pool withdraw/redeem selectors instead burn LP shares for an immediate proportional ETH-plus-spETH payout; identical signatures do not imply identical semantics across deployments.

Each new request accumulates caller pending amount, resets unlockEpoch to currentEpoch+1, and OVERWRITES the receiver for the entire accumulated request. Seven-day epochs plus mutable validatorsDisassembleTime determine claim time; current getter reads 604800 seconds, yielding approximately 7–14 days, while source permits up to 90 days additional delay. Current epoch171 exceeds withdrawalsStartEpoch10. No request cancellation, immutable recipient, fixed maturity or validator-exit/liquidity guarantee is asserted.

completeWithdraw() claims only msg.sender pending ledger to its recorded receiver (zero receiver falls back to caller), requires unlock time and sufficient native ETH, decrements totalPendingWithdraw and deletes caller request before sending ETH. Failed receiver payment or insufficient funds reverts. It cannot independently select another claim owner or change receiver.

swapmpETHforETH(amount,minOut) on the documented liquid pool is current spETH FAST unstaking despite legacy method naming: pulls caller spETH under existing allowance and pays native ETH only to caller. minOut bounds net output. Dynamic fee floors spETH amount*feeBps/10000, then converts net shares to ETH; current reads minFee25, maxFee1000, treasuryFee2500 and targetLiquidity21 ETH. Governance may change these; implementation allows maxFee up to1000 and treasury fraction up to7000 bps. Full pre-fee gross ETH must fit tracked pool liquidity; no deadline or guaranteed reserves exists.

Role/admin/upgrades, initializer/recovery distributor, reports and validator activation, signatures, approvals/transfers and staking-contract-only swaps/validator funding remain excluded. Mutable oracle, validator, treasury, withdrawal and pool behavior remains outside static metadata guarantees.

This integration uses current Ethereum spETH 0xD06f6a56c5f599cB375B616DF306f32B7F6f4A0E, not compromised legacy mpETH. Current primary deployment and product docs advertise normal ETH staking plus fast and delayed unstaking; current source initialize explicitly replaces balances from the June 17, 2025 incident. No recovery distribution or legacy mint method is admitted. Documentation is normal-product lifecycle evidence, not a new audit, safety assurance or a claim about incident reimbursement.

Current EIP1967 source-service resolution identifies staking implementation 0xD3dB79D2D00A6B82531D8Ccf65C376d9eE9513aC, withdrawal implementation 0xcB894c063c74053c9401ac8FDd9A9f2bb1a03c61 and liquid pool implementation 0xeA9fec1ff24B523424F21eeA5c249f9b29A1AA81. Exact source-service match labels are retained, including non-exact match for Withdrawal implementation. All are upgradeable, and staking admin may change withdrawal and pool dependencies; no persistent implementation binding is implied.

On the staking proxy, depositETH(receiver) funds staking using msg.value; deposit(assets,receiver) and mint(shares,receiver) atomically pull WETH from msg.sender and unwrap it. A minimum 0.01 ETH equivalent applies. Shares may be sourced from the configured liquid pool before new minting. Receiver chooses share ownership and must be intentional; use own wallet for own staking. Existing WETH allowance is required but no approval capability is added.

For staking-token accounting, ETH, WETH and spETH use 18-decimal base units. Vendored ERC4626 conversions use virtual assets and shares: shares=floor(assets*(totalSupply+1)/(totalAssets+1)); mint rounds assets up, withdraw rounds burned shares up, redeem rounds assets down. totalAssets uses updater-reported underlying and signed estimated rewards, not a raw onchain balance or backing proof. Share-rate estimates, losses and fees can change; entry methods have no minimum-shares or deadline parameter.

On the staking proxy, entry fee is taken from the gross shares before transfer to receiver (except pool caller), so returned/event shares and requested mint shares are gross, not guaranteed receiver-net shares. Admin may set depositFee up to 100 bps and rewardFee up to 2000 bps; current explorer reads depositFee=0 and rewardsFee=500. Whitelist is source-enforced on caller when enabled; current explorer reads whitelistEnabled=false, not a future access promise or jurisdiction/eligibility clearance.

On the staking proxy, withdraw(assets,receiver,owner) and redeem(shares,receiver,owner) are ASYNCHRONOUS requests, not immediate WETH/ETH payment: burn owner shares, decrease totalUnderlying and queue ETH owed in Withdrawal. If caller differs from owner it consumes owner share allowance. Critically the queue is keyed to caller, NOT owner: use owner=caller for own positions; allowance does not create an owner-keyed claim. The separately admitted liquid-pool withdraw/redeem selectors instead burn LP shares for an immediate proportional ETH-plus-spETH payout; identical signatures do not imply identical semantics across deployments.

Each new request accumulates caller pending amount, resets unlockEpoch to currentEpoch+1, and OVERWRITES the receiver for the entire accumulated request. Seven-day epochs plus mutable validatorsDisassembleTime determine claim time; current getter reads 604800 seconds, yielding approximately 7–14 days, while source permits up to 90 days additional delay. Current epoch171 exceeds withdrawalsStartEpoch10. No request cancellation, immutable recipient, fixed maturity or validator-exit/liquidity guarantee is asserted.

completeWithdraw() claims only msg.sender pending ledger to its recorded receiver (zero receiver falls back to caller), requires unlock time and sufficient native ETH, decrements totalPendingWithdraw and deletes caller request before sending ETH. Failed receiver payment or insufficient funds reverts. It cannot independently select another claim owner or change receiver.

swapmpETHforETH(amount,minOut) on the documented liquid pool is current spETH FAST unstaking despite legacy method naming: pulls caller spETH under existing allowance and pays native ETH only to caller. minOut bounds net output. Dynamic fee floors spETH amount*feeBps/10000, then converts net shares to ETH; current reads minFee25, maxFee1000, treasuryFee2500 and targetLiquidity21 ETH. Governance may change these; implementation allows maxFee up to1000 and treasury fraction up to7000 bps. Full pre-fee gross ETH must fit tracked pool liquidity; no deadline or guaranteed reserves exists.

Role/admin/upgrades, initializer/recovery distributor, reports and validator activation, signatures, approvals/transfers and staking-contract-only swaps/validator funding remain excluded. The current liquid-unstake pool separately admits LP deposit/depositETH, inherited mint and proportional withdraw/redeem; these are LP capital accounting, not staking-token mint or delayed queue requests. Mutable oracle, validator, treasury, withdrawal and pool behavior remains outside static metadata guarantees.

warnings: Static exact-deployment ABI/source inventory only: not a fresh RPC/storage/runtime identity, liquidity, successful-execution, full-workflow or financial-safety guarantee. Exact grants, canonical calldata/value checks, pauses and independent controls remain mandatory.

Monad143 shMON proxy 0x1B68626dCa36c7fE922fD2d55E4f631d962dE19c currently points to explorer-reported ShMonad implementation 0x8Ee4FF5FF50198dcbB7B882A0781F42724Dd095f. Initial constructor implementation 0xbe59fC165fb8941d6d0De527e58Ff649a6fBe95c is not the reviewed interface. Code and governance can change; current storage/upgrade-authority configuration was not read.

deposit/mint use native MON, not WMON or an ERC20 allowance. MON assets and shMON shares use 18-decimal units. deposit requires msg.value exactly assets; mint requires msg.value exactly the execution-time ceil-rounded previewMint amount, so a prior quote may become stale. Pooled withdrawals/redemptions, their protected variants, requestUnstake and completeUnstake are nonpayable and require zero native value. Separately admitted depositIsolated and depositToZeroYieldTranche also accept native MON with exact-value checks.

Ordinary pooled uncommitted shMON is distinct from the separately admitted isolated-validator and hMON ledger methods, queued policy completions and preauthorized agent exits. No new commitment, policy/agent installation, automatic-top-up configuration, hold authority, delegated-completor approval, ERC20 approval/transfer/permit, recovered-principal extraction, commission or validator-maintenance capability is admitted. Policy-agent exits can consume existing committed and uncommitting funds and configured top-up allowance from uncommitted funds; these financially broad preexisting permissions are prerequisites, not grants made by catalog admission.

Atomic withdraw/redeem burn owner uncommitted shares; caller other than owner needs existing share allowance. Native MON goes to explicit nonzero receiver, which must accept empty-calldata native transfer. Amounts are net MON for withdraw and shMON shares for redeem. Current liquidity, recent-revenue offsets, utilization fee and circuit breaker constrain execution.

Atomic fees follow mutable capped-linear utilization parameters, with a 1 gwei minimum when fees are enabled; that minimum can consume tiny outputs. Ordinary withdraw/redeem have no slippage bound. Protected variants atomically enforce maximum shares burned or minimum MON paid after the nested ordinary operation, reverting the entire transaction on failure. No selected method has a deadline.

requestUnstake burns caller nonzero uncommitted shares immediately and fixes a floor-rounded MON liability using recent-revenue-adjusted exchange rate; requests no longer earn rewards. Same completion epochs merge into up to seven pending buckets plus matured bucket. completionEpoch uses internal protocol epochs, normally native withdrawal delay plus four, with two additional epochs when global redemption capacity is insufficient.

completeUnstake pays every matured caller request directly to caller, leaving later requests queued. Completion requires internal epoch advancement/crank progress and sufficient redemption reserves or atomic-liquidity shortfall coverage; maturity is not a cash or wall-clock guarantee. No request ID, arbitrary receiver, operator approval or cancellation is accepted by these two pooled functions.

Closed mode blocks deposit/mint and traditional request/completion; atomic exits are not closed-gated but remain liquidity/circuit-breaker constrained. Frozen mode affects validator operations and may delay liquidity while ordinary pooled calls are not directly frozen-gated. Owner/governance can change fees, commissions, modes and implementations; documentation describes 3-day upgrade timelocks, not an independently read live timelock attestation.

Share conversion uses virtual +1 assets/shares with floor deposit/redeem and ceil mint/withdraw rounding; recent revenue is included on entry but excluded on exit, so immediate round trips can lose value. No role/KYC check appears on these ordinary implementation entries; source-level permissionlessness does not establish legal or frontend jurisdiction eligibility.
